1. With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.
2.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 13/9/2006 passed in MACC No.6/2006 by the First Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Shajapur whereby a total sum of Rs.2,00,200/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation.
3.

Short facts of the case are that on 12/7/2005 Yogaji Rao (the deceased) was driving the metador bearing registration No.M.P. 09 KB 3208 owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2, going from Shajapur to Dewas.

As soon as the said vehicle reached near A.B. Road, Jalalapur at about 1.00 PM in the noon due to imbalance of the vehicle, it suddenly dashed with Babul tree as a result of which the Yogaji Roa, died on the spot.
The appellants filed an application under Section 163-A of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death.
The application was contested by respondent No.2 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,00,200/- in terms of 2nd Schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act considering the fact that the claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal has awarded only a meager amount of Rs.2,00,200/-.

He by referring to para 14 of the impugned award submits that although the claims tribunal has considered the income of the deceased as Rs.24,000/- per annum i.e. Rs.
Smt.Gayatribai vs Mohd.Naeem on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64372163/
1 2000 per month but after deducting Rs. 800/- for personal expenses, the annual income is taken at Rs. 14,400/- and by applying the multiplier of 13, total compensation for loss of dependency was awarded at Rs.1,87,200/-.

After awarding amount of Rs.2000/- for funeral expenses and Rs.5000/-
for loss of consortium to wife and Rs.2000/- each to 3 children of the deceased for loss of consortium, a total sum of Rs.2,00,200/- has been awarded.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal looking to the fact that the deceased was working as a driver should have awarded at least Rs.5.00 lakhs in terms of the amended provision of Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
In support of his submissions he placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
V / s.
Urmila Halder, 2025 ACJ 244
. He submits that in view of the said judgment this amendment shall have retrospective effect.
He further submits that for funeral expenses and loss of consortium meager amount has been awarded.
The date of accident is 12/7/2005, considering the same atleast Rs.40,000/- should have awarded to each of the four claimants.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company has submitted that the deceased was the driver of the vehicle which caused accident.
He was driving metador bearing registration No.M.P. 09 KB 3208.
He points out that the Insurance Company has filed cross objection thereby raising issue of negligence of driver himself.
He thus prays for setting aside the impugned award.
As regards the income the learned counsel points out that the claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In such section, structured formula for award of compensation is provided in terms of second schedule of the Act.
In the second schedule maximum annual income is prescribed at Rs.40,000/-.

As such the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the income and if the cross objection of the Insurance Company is not entertained then on the question of quantum of compensation, no interference is warranted.

8. He further points out that the quantification of compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act and 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act are two different procedures, which are not only independent to each other but they rest on fault liability in one and no fault liability in the other.
Thus parameters of Section 166 of the M.V. Act cannot be adopted in the proceedings of Section 163- A.
He thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.
9. In the rejoinder submissions, learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the amendment would have retrospective effect.

Thus ceiling of maximum income of Rs.40,000/-
would not come in the way as upto Rs.5,00,000/- compensation can be awarded.
10. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

11. Insofar as the cross objection of the Insurance Company is concerned, the same is not entertainable in view of the fact that the application for claim was filed by the claimants under Smt.Gayatribai vs Mohd.Naeem on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64372163/
2 Section 163-A of the M.V. Act.

This position has already been cleared by the Hon'ble Apex Court by its authoritative pronouncement in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s. Sunil Kumar & Anr .

sentences.text: In this view of the matter the cross objection of the Insurance Co. is hereby dismissed.
12. As regards the compensation to the claimants it is seen from the record that the accident occurred on 12/7/2005 and the impugned award was passed on 13/9/2006.
The award has been passed long before the amended in Section 163-A of the M.V. Act.

The provision of Section 163-A was amended with effect from 22/5/2018 ie., after more than 12 years of the accident and in this view of the matter, this Court is not inclined to grant benefit of amendment in Section 163-A of the M.V. Act in the year 2018.
Thus on this count interference in the impugned award is hereby declined.

However, it is seen from the record that the claims tribunal has awarded only a meager sum of Rs.2000/- each to all three claimants, under the head of loss of consortium and to the wife of the deceased an amount of Rs.5000/- has been awarded.
Apart from this in the head of funeral expenses only Rs.2000/- has been awarded.

13. Though it is correct that present is a case of structured formula granting compensation as per second schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act but this provision of Section 163-A and second schedule has been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kurvan Ansari alias Kurvan Ali Vs.
ShyamKishore Murmu & Anr., 2022 (1) SCC 317,

entities.text:
Kurvan Ansari alias Kurvan Ali Vs.
ShyamKishore Murmu & Anr., 2022 (1) SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and after considering the inflation in the cost of living and devaluation in the value of rupee not an award of Rs.40,000/- each towards filial consortium and an amount of Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses was awarded by the Hon'ble Apex Court in terms of para 16 of the said case.
In the said case, the accident occurred on 06.09.2004 and in the present case, the date of death is subsequent to date of death of that case before the Supreme Court.

Thus, this Court is of considered view, in the present case also the appellants are entitled for amount of spousal as well as parental consortium at Rs.40,000/- each and 5 MA-3853-2006 enhancement of funeral expenses at Rs.15,000/-.
14.

In this view of the matter, all the four claimants are hereby awarded the compensation for loss of consortium at Rs.40,000/- each which comes to Rs.1,60,000/- and for funeral expenses an amount of Rs.15,000/- is awarded.
The total of which would come to Rs.1,75,000/-.
Out of this amount the already awarded total amount under these heads at Rs.13,000/- is deducted.
As such the remaining amount of Rs.1,62,000/- is to be paid to the appellants over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount of Rs.1,62,000/- shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the claims tribunal.
15. Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
